instruction: Attribute Domain Transfer `scene.blend` contains a single mesh object `Plate` (a flat subdivided plane lying on z=0). In this image, the Blender executable is `/opt/blender/blender`; use it to open `scene.blend`. The mesh carries one custom named attribute: `material_id`, type INT, domain FACE. Its values are in {1, 2, 3} and are distributed so that all three values appear. Create a NEW named attribute `material_id_vert`, type INT, on the VERTEX (POINT) domain. For every vertex, its value must equal the MAXIMUM of the `material_id` values of that vertex's incident faces. `max` is both the aggregation rule and the tie-break: if two incident faces share an id, the result is that id; if they differ, the larger integer wins. The original face-domain `material_id` attribute must be preserved unchanged. No geometry changes: vertex count, face count, per-vertex coordinates, and object location must be identical to the initial file. Save the result as `answer.blend`. Requirements: 1. Output scene contains exactly one mesh object named `Plate` at world origin. 2. Vertex count, face count, per-vertex coordinates, and axis-aligned bounding box are unchanged from `scene.blend`. 3. A FACE-domain INT attribute named `material_id` still exists with the original values intact, and all three ids {1, 2, 3} appear on it. 4. A POINT-domain INT attribute named `material_id_vert` exists (newly created), distinct from the face-domain `material_id`. 5. For every vertex v, `material_id_vert[v]` equals max(material_id[f] : f is a face incident to v). 6. All three ids {1, 2, 3} appear on the vertex-domain attribute. Read the face-domain values and write the vertex-domain values; do not infer from vertex coordinates.
